title: Kamphaeng Phet 3 Days 2 Nights — Old City, Khlong Lan & Mae Wong
metaDesc: A 3-day 2-night Kamphaeng Phet itinerary in Thailand: walk the UNESCO Historical Park, Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Chang Rop, swim at Khlong Lan Waterfall, and end in Mae Wong forest — with real restaurants, real entry fees, and travel tips.

ogTitle: Kamphaeng Phet 3 Days 2 Nights — Old City, Khlong Lan, Mae Wong
ogDesc: A 3-day 2-night Kamphaeng Phet trip covering the UNESCO old city, Khlong Lan Waterfall, and Mae Wong forest — with timings, costs, and real local restaurants.
intro: Kamphaeng Phet is a town most people drive straight past, but give it 3 days and 2 nights and you'll get all three sides it's known for: a UNESCO old city that's quiet and still uncrowded, Khlong Lan Waterfall just a short drive away, and the Mae Wong forest for anyone who loves nature. This plan sequences everything so the driving flows, with real timings, real entry fees, and the places locals actually eat.

blocks.html: Before we start, a quick lay of the land. Kamphaeng Phet splits into three main directions for sightseeing: the town and the Nakhon Chum side, home to the Historical Park, most of the hotels, markets, and restaurants · Khlong Lan district, about 55–65 km to the southwest, with Khlong Lan Waterfall and Khlong Nam Lai Waterfall · and Mae Wong / Pang Sila Thong district, the big forest to the south. So this plan spreads out one direction at a time, instead of running back and forth in a single day.

This trip works best if you have your own car or a rental, because Khlong Lan and Mae Wong are far from town and public transport is inconvenient. Inside the Historical Park you can easily walk or cycle around — it's a big area but the paths are flat and there's plenty of shade. If you're not driving yourself, hiring a car by the day for the Khlong Lan and Mae Wong legs works out better.

blocks.text: Day 1 — UNESCO Old City + Nakhon Chum

blocks.html: Give the first day to the Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai. What sets it apart from other old cities is that most of the ruins are built from reddish-brown laterite, sitting among tall trees — shady and quiet, easy to wander all day.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: UNESCO old city and the Nakhon Chum retro market

items.activity: Start inside the city walls — Wat Phra Kaeo at the heart of the park
items.note: Park open 08:00–16:30 daily · Wat Phra Kaeo was the royal temple at the centre of town, with rows of laterite stupas and Buddha images — the spot most people picture first when they think of Kamphaeng Phet.

items.activity: Wat Phra That, right next to Wat Phra Kaeo
items.note: A bell-shaped stupa on a square base, close enough to walk straight over — no need to move the car.

items.activity: Kamphaeng Phet National Museum
items.note: See bronze Buddha images and artefacts unearthed around the city — good background before heading out to the Aranyik zone. Entry for Thais is around 20 THB.

items.activity: Lunch break — beef noodles / braised chicken noodles in town
items.note: There are several noodle shops in town. Try the old-recipe stewed beef noodles or the braised chicken, both local specialities.

items.activity: Head to the Aranyik zone (outside the city walls) — Wat Chang Rop
items.note: A large stupa with a base ringed by 68 stucco elephants — a highlight of Kamphaeng Phet, set in shady forest.

items.activity: Wat Phra Si Iriyabot — the four-posture Buddhas on a laterite wall
items.note: It once had standing, walking, seated, and reclining Buddhas on all four sides; today the standing figure is the most complete — a rare piece of craftsmanship.

items.activity: Wat Sing / Wat Awat Yai in the Aranyik zone
items.note: Walk or cycle on within the same zone. The laterite wells and stupa bases still show their structure clearly, the crowds are thin, and the photos come out great.

items.activity: Cross the Ping River to the Nakhon Chum side — Wat Phra Borommathat, Nakhon Chum
items.note: A newly restored Burmese-style stupa with a gilded top — unlike the ruins in the park, this is a working temple still in active use.

items.activity: Nakhon Chum retro market (Fri–Sat–Sun only)
items.note: Opens from around 3pm. Vendors dress in Thai costume, with local food and old-style sweets. If your dates line up, it makes a great dinner to close the first day.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park is split into the area inside the city walls and the Aranyik zone outside town. The two are a fair distance apart, so driving or cycling beats walking. Bring water and a hat because the midday sun is strong — though the Aranyik zone has plenty of shade, which helps a lot. And if you want to catch the Nakhon Chum retro market, check whether your visit falls on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday.

blocks.text: Recommended restaurants for the whole trip

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet is known first and foremost for beef noodles and braised chicken. The town's signature thing to take home is the egg banana (kluai khai) — eaten fresh and also turned into candied or stewed banana. These are real, open spots that locals actually go to, easy to drop into along your route through the day.

items.name: Good View Braised Chicken Noodles
items.blurb: A long-running shop in town that comes up often when people talk about noodles in Kamphaeng Phet. The braised chicken is tender, the broth well-balanced, and there's khanom chin and chicken rice on the menu too. Good for breakfast or lunch before heading into the old city.
items.meta: Thesa 2 Road, in town · breakfast–lunch · from 45–70 THB

items.name: Nakhon Chum Stewed Beef Noodles
items.blurb: An old-recipe beef noodle shop on the Nakhon Chum side that's been part of the town for a long time. The beef is stewed until soft, the broth is rich and loaded with toppings — a taste the older generation here grew up with.
items.meta: Nakhon Chum area · breakfast–lunch · from 45–65 THB

items.name: Baan Rim Nam, Nakhon Chum
items.blurb: A riverside restaurant on the Nakhon Chum side of the Ping River — sit in the cool breeze with a river view. The menu runs to Thai dishes and river fish, making for an easy dinner after a full day of sightseeing.
items.meta: Riverside, Nakhon Chum · lunch–dinner · 80–250 THB per dish

items.name: Nakhon Chum Retro Market
items.blurb: A walking street market with old-town atmosphere — vendors in Thai costume, plenty of local savoury and sweet dishes, and traditional snacks to sample, all in one place. Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday only, from around 3pm.
items.meta: Nakhon Chum · Fri–Sun afternoon–evening · 20–60 THB per item

items.name: Kamphaeng Phet Egg Banana Souvenirs
items.blurb: The egg banana is the province's signature product — small fruit with thin skin and a sweet, fragrant flavour. Beyond eating it fresh, there's candied banana, stewed banana, and banana chips to take home. Find them at souvenir shops in town and during the Egg Banana Festival in late September.
items.meta: Souvenir shops in town · gifts · from 40–120 THB

items.name: Riverside Cafés
items.blurb: The town has several newer cafés along the Ping River and around the town centre — good for a coffee break after walking the old city. Some have a river-view corner to sit and relax.
items.meta: Riverside / in town · all day · coffee 55–90 THB

blocks.text: Day 2 — Khlong Lan and Khlong Nam Lai Waterfalls

blocks.html: Day two heads out of town to the southwest toward Khlong Lan National Park, about 55–65 km away. The highlight is Khlong Lan Waterfall, which spreads down a tall cliff in a wide curtain. It's a short walk from the car park to the falls, so it suits anyone who wants to swim and relax in the forest without a hard hike.

items.activity: Leave town for Khlong Lan National Park (~55–65 km)
items.note: About 1–1.5 hours driving yourself · park open 08:30–16:30 · if you don't have a car, hiring one by the day is more convenient than the local bus.

items.activity: Arrive at the park, buy tickets at the gate
items.note: Adults 40 THB, children 20 THB · car 30 THB, motorbike 20 THB.

items.activity: Walk and swim at Khlong Lan Waterfall
items.note: The path from the car park to the falls is short and family-friendly · the falls are large with a wide curtain, and there's plenty of strong water late in the rainy season.

items.activity: Lunch at the park welfare shop / community eateries
items.note: There are eateries near the park and in the surrounding villages, but options are limited — bring some snacks and water in the car just in case.

items.activity: Drive on to Khlong Nam Lai Waterfall (same park)
items.note: A low, tiered rock waterfall flowing over boulders — easy for strolling and photos, with a different feel from Khlong Lan.

items.activity: Stop at the Kiu Krathing viewpoint or melon / fruit farms along the way
items.note: This stretch of road has mountain viewpoints and seasonal fruit orchards — a good spot to stop for a snack.

items.activity: Drive back to town
items.note: Arrive around dusk, rest, and find dinner in town or on the Nakhon Chum side.

blocks.title: Day 2 tip
blocks.html: Khlong Lan Waterfall is at its most beautiful and full from late rainy season into early winter (October–December); in the dry season the water drops. If you're set on swimming, aim for this window — and check the park's announcements before you go, because during heavy rains the flow can get strong and the swimming area is sometimes closed temporarily for safety.

The last day switches to deep forest at Mae Wong National Park, a vast forest straddling the Kamphaeng Phet–Nakhon Sawan border. There are easy roadside viewpoints to stop at, plus a longer trek up to Mokoju Peak, the park's highest point and a multi-day hike for the genuinely fit. For this 3-day 2-night plan, we focus on the spots you can hit in a single day before heading home.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Mae Wong nature before heading home

items.activity: Check out + set off for Mae Wong National Park
items.note: The headquarters is in the south of the province, about 1.5–2 hours' drive from town · check opening times and routes with the park in advance.

items.activity: Arrive at park HQ, register + buy tickets
items.note: Adult/child entry and vehicle fees follow the national park rates, paid at the gate.

items.activity: Stop at roadside viewpoints on the Khlong Lan–Umphang road (the Mae Wong stretch)
items.note: This stretch of road has sea-of-mountains viewpoints at intervals — good for photos and a lungful of forest air.

items.activity: Walk a short nature trail around HQ
items.note: The trails near HQ suit anyone not here for a hard hike — forest and streams with a nice atmosphere.

items.activity: Lunch — packed meal / food you brought
items.note: Eateries inside the park are limited, so bring your own water and supplies.

items.activity: Leave the park, drive home
items.note: Allow enough time to clear the mountain road before dark, since some sections have no lighting and the road is winding.

blocks.title: Before you go to Mae Wong
blocks.html: Mokoju Peak is a long-distance trek that takes several days and is open seasonally (usually in the cool season); it requires a booking and a guide, and is not a spot you can drop into for a single-day walk. On a short trip, focus on the roadside viewpoints and the short trails around HQ instead — and always call the park first to check which areas are open during your visit.

blocks.text: When's the best time to visit Kamphaeng Phet

blocks.html: The best weather is November–February — the sun isn't harsh, the old city is comfortable to walk, and the Khlong Lan and Mae Wong forests are still green from the rains. If you want the waterfalls at their fullest, go in late rainy to early winter (October–December), when Khlong Lan Waterfall has the most water. For local flavour, the Egg Banana Festival runs from mid to late September each year, with lots of food and community products — but it draws crowds and hotels fill fast, so book ahead. The hot season (March–May) brings strong sun and low water at the falls, so start sightseeing early and rest at midday.

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: Yes, and it fits nicely. Day one walks the UNESCO Historical Park — both the in-town and Aranyik zones — plus a stop at Nakhon Chum. Day two heads out to swim at Khlong Lan and Khlong Nam Lai Waterfalls. Day three closes with nature at Mae Wong before the drive home. You get both the history and the nature side without rushing.

faq.q: Can I visit Kamphaeng Phet without my own car?
faq.a: Within the Historical Park and the town you can manage with local hired transport or by renting a bicycle to ride around. But Khlong Lan and Mae Wong are far and public transport is inconvenient — hiring a car by the day or renting one is much more flexible.

faq.q: What time does Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park open?
faq.a: It's open daily, 08:00–16:30. It splits into the area inside the city walls (such as Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Phra That) and the Aranyik zone outside town (such as Wat Chang Rop and Wat Phra Si Iriyabot). Entry for Thais is around 20 THB per zone, and you should allow a full day because the area is large.

faq.q: Can you swim at Khlong Lan Waterfall, and when is the water highest?
faq.a: Yes, you can swim, and the walk from the car park to the falls is short and family-friendly. The water is fullest and most beautiful from late rainy to early winter (October–December); in the dry season it drops. Check the park's announcements before you go, because during heavy flow the swimming area is sometimes closed temporarily.

faq.q: Is Mae Wong good for a short trip, and do you have to hike up Mokoju?
faq.a: It's good for a short trip if you stick to the roadside viewpoints and the short trails around HQ — you don't need to climb Mokoju. Mokoju Peak is a multi-day trek that's open seasonally and requires a booking with a guide. Call the park first to check which areas are open during your visit.
